memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He said to Aaron, 'What did these people do to you, that you led them into such great sin?' 'Do not be angry, my lord,' Aaron answered. 'You know how prone these people are to evil. They said to me, "Make us gods who will go before us..."'" - Exod 32:21-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Aaron's answer is painfully familiar. He blames the people. He blames the circumstances. He tells Moses not to be angry. What he never says is, "I did wrong."

We are experts at this. "I was under pressure." "You know what they are like." "Anyone would have done the same." Every excuse contains just enough truth to feel reasonable, and just enough evasion to avoid repentance.

There is a real difference between explaining and confessing. Explaining protects us. Confessing frees us. Aaron gives an explanation; God was waiting for a confession.

David shows us the better way: "Against you, you only, have I sinned" (Ps 51:4). No blame-shifting, no context, no softening. Just honesty before God.

And here is the mercy of the gospel: we can afford to be honest. If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just and will forgive us and purify us (1 John 1:9). We do not have to build a case for ourselves. Christ has already borne the verdict. Excuses are for people with no Saviour.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What is your most common excuse when confronted?
2. Where have you been explaining rather than confessing?
3. What would honest confession look like for you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I stop making excuses. I have sinned, and I need Your mercy. Thank You for forgiving me in Christ. Amen.
